title: OpenStax says speech-sound discrimination narrows to the languages around the baby by about 1 year
summary: OpenStax says babies first tell apart sounds of many languages, and by about 1 year they discriminate the phonemes of the languages around them.
body: OpenStax Psychology 7.2 says babies can tell speech sounds apart early, including sounds that do not occur in the languages around them. It says that by about 1 year they discriminate the phonemes used in the language or languages in their environment. The section cites Jensen, 2011, and Werker and Lalonde, 1988, and Werker and Tees, 1984. Those papers were not opened for this card. The claim here is the textbook's summary, in the CC BY 4.0 first edition, not a new experiment.
